name: fibonacci_exact_n1000
description: Exact non-modular integer Fibonacci F_1000 benchmark for FOL-Zinc/Zinc comparison.
soundness_note: This compact direct benchmark preserves the exact Fibonacci recurrence over the integers, but treats the canonical structural FOL rows C1=k, C3=k-1, and C4=k-2 as public relation structure rather than private witness variables. The private witness row is C2=fib(k). Nothing is reduced modulo 2^64.

zkfol.paper_reference: Trace-specialised exact-integer version of the Fibonacci FOL example. The open-science appendix of the paper lists Fibonacci among the bundled implemented FOL examples; the direct mode here preserves the integer witness semantics but avoids expanding every value into paper B-bit lookup variables for large benchmark n.
zkfol.mathematical_description: Exact integer Fibonacci trace: fib(1)=fib(2)=1 and fib(k)=fib(k-1)+fib(k-2), proving public relation constant F_1000.
zkfol.witness_convention: Compact profile: C2=fib(k) is private. Structural FOL rows are implicit public relation structure: C1=k, C3=pointer to k-1, and C4=pointer to k-2; for the two base columns, both pointer rows point to column 1.

structural_rows.C3: implicit public structure C3(k)=1 for k<=2 else k-1
structural_rows.C4: implicit public structure C4(k)=1 for k<=2 else k-2

reference_report.note: Compact direct trace-specialised CCS generated from the Fibonacci witness convention. For n>20, per-column zero lists are omitted to keep metadata small.

exposition.what_this_file_is: A self-contained exact-integer Fibonacci benchmark input for the Rust Zinc runner. It uses the compact direct profile: only the Fibonacci value row is private, while canonical index/pointer rows are public relation structure.
concrete_statement: Output size: 694 bits; no modulo 2^64 reduction is used.
Public claim: n and the exact Fibonacci output are public relation constants in the exported JSON.
exposition.what_is_being_proved: Knowledge of the exact integer Fibonacci trace C2[1..1000], with C2[1]=C2[2]=1, C2[k]=C2[k-1]+C2[k-2], and final public relation constant C2[1000]=F_1000. The canonical FOL index and pointer rows are fixed as public relation structure in this compact profile.
exposition.why_zero_matters: Every exported CCS row is an integer equality. Passing the local relation check means the exact integer trace satisfies the Fibonacci recurrence.

pipeline.meaning: Rows C1..C4 encode k, fib(k), k-1 pointer, and k-2 pointer.
C1/C3/C4 are canonical public structure; only C2 is private witness data.
Each base, recurrence, and public final equality is exported as <left,z>*1=<right,z>.
The Rust runner checks the integer relation, pads CCS dimensions, then invokes Zinc.

benchmarking_notes: This is exact, non-modular arithmetic. It is deliberately not a mod-2^64 match for RISC Zero's documented fib bench.
The compact profile is the fastest package default for n=10000 because it removes redundant private structural rows and pointer checks.
Use --fib-profile full if you want the older four-row trace-specialised relation with explicit private C1/C3/C4 rows.

example_summary.name: fibonacci_exact_n1000
example_summary.mathematical_description: Proves public exact F_1000 with fib(1)=fib(2)=1.
example_summary.witness_convention: Compact profile: private C2=fib(k); implicit public C1=k, C3=k-1, C4=k-2.
example_summary.paper_reference: Trace-specialised exact-integer version of the Fibonacci FOL example. The open-science appendix of the paper lists Fibonacci among the bundled implemented FOL examples; the direct mode here preserves the integer witness semantics but avoids expanding every value into paper B-bit lookup variables for large benchmark n.

benchmark_claim.description: Public relation constants bind n=1000 and exact F_1000; arithmetic is over the integers, not modulo 2^64. Compact direct rows are positive-oriented equalities left*1=right.
concrete_statement: Output size: 694 bits; no modulo 2^64 reduction is used.

exact_arithmetic.modulus_note: No modular reduction is used in this FOL-Zinc benchmark.
exact_arithmetic.fibonacci_indexing: fib(1)=fib(2)=1, equivalent to standard F_n with F_0=0,F_1=1 for n>=1.

risc0_comparator.official_benchmark_note: RISC Zero documentation says this benchmark computes the 100th, 1000th, and 10000th Fibonacci numbers modulo 2^64, ten times for each, with separate execution and proving statistics. This FOL-Zinc instance intentionally keeps exact integer arithmetic instead.

benchmark_case.note: exact non-modular integer F_1000; same n-value as RISC Zero fib benchmark but not mod 2^64
benchmark_case.comparison_warning: RISC Zero's documented fib benchmark is modulo 2^64; this FOL-Zinc input is exact integer arithmetic.

zinc_constraint_summary.constraint_model: integer R1CS encoded as Zinc CCS_Z
zinc_constraint_summary.degree_explanation: Zinc receives R1CS/CCS rows of the form <A,z>*<B,z>=<C,z>, so the declared CCS degree is 2. After public inputs and the constant-one coordinate are fixed, some specialised rows simplify to degree 1.
zinc_constraint_summary.bit_bound_explanation: bit_bound_delta is the largest absolute bit length among public input values, private witness values, and integer constraint coefficients materialised by this adapter. It is the practical delta-style bound for the exported integer relation, not a requirement that Zinc's sampled prime exceed every value.
